## unicefData

[unicefData](https://github.com/unicef-drp/unicefData) is an open data and analytics toolkit led by UNICEF's Office of the Chief Statistician. It gives R, Python and Stata users a consistent interface to the UNICEF Data Warehouse over the SDMX API: automatic pagination, caching, country name lookups, metadata vintages, and full coverage of the child-related SDG indicators.

**Role:** contributor, with [João Pedro Azevedo](https://jpazvd.github.io/) (lead author and maintainer), Lucas Rodrigues and Yang Liu.

| Language | Registry | Install |
|---|---|---|
| R | [CRAN: unicefData](https://cran.r-project.org/package=unicefData) | `install.packages("unicefData")` |
| Python | [PyPI: unicefdata](https://pypi.org/project/unicefdata/) | `pip install unicefdata` |
| Stata | [SSC: unicefdata](https://ideas.repec.org/c/boc/bocode/s459598.html) | `ssc install unicefdata` |

Source code, issues and documentation: [github.com/unicef-drp/unicefData](https://github.com/unicef-drp/unicefData).

## unequal (R package)

**unequal** measures inequality and decomposes it by population subgroup, income source, regression terms and over time, with every estimator tied to the equation it implements and competing methods offered side by side. It covers the Gini family and generalized entropy indices, Lorenz and concentration curves, Lorenz dominance tests, Kuznets curves, tax progressivity and redistribution, mobility, poverty (FGT, Watts, Sen, growth and redistribution decompositions), relative deprivation, inequality of opportunity, concentration indices for health outcomes, estimation from grouped data, and inference by bootstrap, jackknife and linearisation with complex survey designs.

**Role:** author and maintainer. Development version, not yet on CRAN.

[Guide (PDF)](unequal-guide.pdf){.pub-link} *Inequality analysis with the unequal package: a guide for economists and sociologists*, 40+ pages with worked examples on a household survey.

## Research code and replication materials

Public repositories with the code behind my papers and working projects. Microdata (RLMS-HSE, PIAAC, MICS) is not redistributed; each repository documents how to obtain it.

| Repository | Language | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [wages-ncs-rlms](https://github.com/karavan88/wages-ncs-rlms) | R | Returns to non-cognitive skills across the wage distribution: occupational sorting, supervision and trait-specific pathways (RLMS-HSE 2017–2025). |
| [happiness-premium-rlms](https://github.com/karavan88/happiness-premium-rlms) | R | Beyond the happiness premium: personality, affect and labor market outcomes (RLMS-HSE 2017–2025). |
| [LM-NonCognSkills-PIAAC](https://github.com/karavan88/LM-NonCognSkills-PIAAC) | R | Causal mediation study of the returns to non-cognitive skills in PIAAC Cycle 2. |
| [NCSJobSatisfPIAAC](https://github.com/karavan88/NCSJobSatisfPIAAC) | R | Are non-cognitive skills rewarded with job satisfaction net of pay? PIAAC Cycle 2, 23 countries. |
| [EduProdFunctionPISA](https://github.com/karavan88/EduProdFunctionPISA) | R | Education production functions from cross-sectional PISA data with mixed-effects models. |
| [DigitalSkillsGender](https://github.com/karavan88/DigitalSkillsGender) | R | Replication code for the household fixed-effects analysis of gender gaps in digital skills (Heliyon, 2024). |
| [MICS-FLS-Data-Harmonization](https://github.com/karavan88/MICS-FLS-Data-Harmonization) | R | Harmonization of foundational learning skills variables across MICS surveys. |
| [PredictSDG4Scenarios](https://github.com/karavan88/PredictSDG4Scenarios) | R | Scenario projections of country performance on SDG 4 education indicators. |
| [NonCognitiveSkillsNEET](https://github.com/karavan88/NonCognitiveSkillsNEET) | R | Analysis behind "How far are NEET youth falling behind in their non-cognitive skills?" (Economies, 2024). |

:::

All repositories are on [GitHub](https://github.com/karavan88).
